subject: CSA intake: control shepherding and artifact tagging plan
messages:
From: Lisa Carter <lisa.carter@cloudcrest.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Cloudcrest Security <security@cloudcrest.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: CSA intake - tenant boundaries + runtime telemetry request

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for agreeing to help with our CSA review. We're working through the CAIQ and have a couple of focused asks where we need artifact evidence and control owners:

- Tenant boundary/tenancy model: a short mapping that shows where tenant isolation is enforced (compute, storage, and networking) and any compensating controls.
- Runtime telemetry: examples of the telemetry we retain for inference requests (sampling level, retention window, and a redacted log sample).

If you can provide a control-to-artifact index (spreadsheet) and attach a 10–20 line redacted log sample that demonstrates request-scoped fields (timestamps, tenant-id, request-id), that would help speed up our scoring. Ideally we get this by end of next week (2026-10-11).

Also please let us know who the control owners are for the tenancy and telemetry controls so we can mark them as points of contact in the CAIQ.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Carter
Security Programs Manager
Cloudcrest Solutions

--

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T11:46:00-04:00
Subject: Re: CSA intake - tenant boundaries + runtime telemetry request

Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the clarity. We're on it. Quick notes and ask for scope confirmation:

1) Tenant boundary: we'll produce a compact control mapping that calls out enforcement boundaries (hypervisor/container runtime, network ACLs, object storage policies) and link to the design doc. Expect a matrix with column headers: CSA control id, Redwood control id, artifact, owner, evidence link.

2) Runtime telemetry: we'll include a redacted log sample with masking applied to PII and full tenant IDs replaced with hashed tokens. We'll also include the retention policy excerpt and sampling config.

3) Owners: Marissa (cc'd) will take lead on owner assignment for tenancy controls; Priyom will validate runtime instrumentation snippets.

Action plan from our side:
- 2026-10-06: internal artifact harvest and owner roster (spreadsheet).
- 2026-10-08: initial CAIQ crosswalk & evidence zip to you (spreadsheet + log sample).
- 2026-10-11: finalized evidence and sign-off.

Can you confirm you are scoped to the standard CAIQ (v4.0) and whether you need any additional runtime replay artifacts (we can provide a short 30s replay trace if desired)?

I'll attach the initial mapping matrix (redwood_csa_matrix_v0.1.xlsx) in the next internal message; for the external exchange we'll push a curated bundle with links.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / Priyom —

Uploading the first pass of the mapping into the drive folder (link below). Notes for the sprint:

- redwood_csa_matrix_v0.1.xlsx (attached to internal bucket): has preliminary mappings for CCM controls relevant to tenant isolation and telemetry. Column definitions included in sheet 'README'.
- owner_roster_v2.csv: table of owner handles (control id -> owner email). Marissa will shepherd tenancy controls (CCM-2, CCM-5 series).
- runtime_log_sample.txt: synthetic but redaction-patterned sample log showing timestamp, request_id, tenant_hash, action, latency_ms.

Priyom — can you: 
- Add a brief note in the matrix under column "instrumentation_proof" referencing the middleware trace point and a short snippet of the log query used to extract the sample.
- Confirm the retention window statement (we currently hold request telemetry at 90 days; some aggregated metrics for 13 months). If you spot any wording that would be problematic for auditors, flag it.

I'll prepare the external zip for Lisa containing: redwood_csa_matrix_v0.1.xlsx, runtime_log_sample.txt, owner_roster_v2.csv and a short narrative PDF that explains our tenancy model.

Hi Evelyn & Marissa —

Perfect, this plan looks good. CAIQ v4.0 is the schema we're using. The artifacts you listed sound sufficient for the initial review; the redaction approach you described is acceptable to our audit team.

Two small asks: 
1) Please include a single-line authority statement in the matrix confirming that the owner roster has been reviewed by the named owners (e.g., "Owner reviewed on 2026-10-06 by Priyom Das").
2) For runtime telemetry, include the exact query used to pull the sample (redacted to remove internal hostnames) so our auditors can replicate the extraction on the sample set.

If you hit delays, let me know — we can stretch the internal review by a couple of days, but it's helpful to keep the target window.

Thanks again — we'll be watching for the external bundle.

Regards,
Lisa Carter
Security Programs Manager
Cloudcrest Solutions
